1. (Currently amended) A method for controlling a flow of air, the method comprising: establishing a level of vacuum in a booster device by generating the flow of air from the booster device using a pump; determining whether the level of vacuum in the booster device has reached a predetermined value; and terminating the flow of air from the booster device when the level of vacuum in the booster device has reached the predetermined value, __wherein the pump is controlled to reduce parasitic load on an engine driving the pump__.

2. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1, wherein said terminating the flow of air is accomplished via a directional control valve, such that a pressure differential across the pump is reduced, __and wherein the directional control valve is activated based on a sensor signal indicating the predetermined vacuum level has been reached__.

3. (Currently amended) The method of claim 2, wherein said terminating the flow of air includes changing the direction of the flow of air and closing a flow path between the pump and the booster device, __such that the pump is decoupled from the booster device__.

4. (Currently amended) The method of claim 3, wherein said changing the direction of the flow of air includes opening a flow path between a negative pressure chamber of the pump and a positive pressure chamber of the pump, __thereby allowing the pump to recirculate air internally__.

5. (Currently amended) The method of claim 3, wherein said changing the direction of the flow of air includes opening a path for a flow of air between the pump and the atmosphere, __thereby venting the pump to atmospheric pressure__.

6. (Currently amended) The method of claim 5, further comprising filtering the flow of air between the atmosphere and the pump via a filter, __wherein the filter prevents contaminants from entering the pump during venting__.

7. (Original) The method of claim 1, wherein the booster device is a vacuum servo booster for an automobile braking system.

8. (Currently amended) A system for controlling a flow of air, the system comprising: a booster device configured to provide a vacuum assist when a level of vacuum has been established in the device; a pump configured to establish the level of vacuum in the booster device by generating the flow of air from the booster device; a directional control valve adapted to terminate the flow of air from the booster device when the level of vacuum in the booster device has reached a predetermined value, such that a pressure differential across the pump is reduced; and __a control module configured to activate the directional control valve based on detection of the predetermined vacuum level__.

9. (Currently amended) The system of claim 8, wherein the directional control valve is further adapted to change the direction of the flow of air and close a flow path between the pump and the booster device, __such that the pump is decoupled from the booster device__.

10. (Currently amended) The system of claim 9, wherein to change the direction of the flow of air the directional control valve opens a flow path between a negative pressure chamber of the pump and a positive pressure chamber of the pump, __thereby allowing the pump to recirculate air internally__.

11. (Currently amended) The system of claim 9, wherein to change the direction of the flow of air the directional control valve opens a flow path between the pump and the atmosphere, __thereby venting the pump to atmospheric pressure__.

12. (Currently amended) The system of claim 11, further comprising a filter adapted for filtering a flow of air between the atmosphere and the pump, __wherein the filter prevents contaminants from entering the pump during venting__.

13. (Original) The system of claim 8, wherein the booster device is a vacuum servo booster for an automobile braking system.

14. (Currently amended) A motor vehicle comprising: an internal combustion engine; a booster device configured to provide a vacuum assist when a level of vacuum has been established in the device; and a system for controlling a flow of air from the booster device, the system including: a pump configured to establish the level of vacuum in the booster device by generating the flow of air from the booster device; a directional control valve adapted to terminate the flow of air from the booster device when the level of vacuum in the booster device has reached a predetermined value, such that a pressure differential across the pump and a parasitic load on the engine are reduced; and __a control module configured to activate the directional control valve based on detection of the predetermined vacuum level__.

15. (Currently amended) The vehicle of claim 14, wherein the directional control valve is further adapted to change the direction of the flow of air and close a flow path between the pump and the booster device, __such that the pump is decoupled from the booster device__.

16. (Currently amended) The vehicle of claim 15, wherein to change the direction of the flow of air the directional control valve opens a flow path between a negative pressure chamber of the pump and a positive pressure chamber of the pump, __thereby allowing the pump to recirculate air internally__.

17. (Currently amended) The vehicle of claim 15, wherein to change the direction of the flow of air the directional control valve opens a flow path between the pump and the atmosphere, __thereby venting the pump to atmospheric pressure__.

18. (Currently amended) The vehicle of claim 17, further comprising a filter adapted for filtering the flow of air between the atmosphere and the pump, __wherein the filter prevents contaminants from entering the pump during venting__.

19. (Original) The vehicle of claim 14, further comprising a braking system, wherein the booster device is a vacuum servo booster for the braking system.

20. (Original) The vehicle of claim 14, wherein the engine is a compression-ignition type.
